summary: Round 2 re-review of all 8 units. All round-1 fixes were verified in the packets: the LAST callout, numbered list, summary and q009 now state the Association of Anaesthetists regimen (20% lipid 1.5 mL/kg over 1 minute then 15 mL/kg/h, bolus repeatable up to twice, infusion up to 30 mL/kg/h, 105 mL for 70 kg, arrest modifications of adrenaline 1 microgram/kg or less, no vasopressin, calcium channel blockers or beta-blockers, prolonged resuscitation); dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg is added; preoperative-risk q009 now restricts bridging to high thrombotic risk; managing-chronic-pain q002 is re-posed with amitriptyline as the single defensible key; and the NG193/NG59 spinal-injection caveat is present. All numeric keys were recomputed in Python and are correct (cylinder 40 and 37.5 min, 105 mL, BMI 35.9 and 34.3, fasting 45 and 15 min, MAP 58 and 68, adrenaline 0.5 and 5 mL, lidocaine 20/50/33 mL, bupivacaine 30/48 mL, PCA 12/9 mg/h, 40% and 37.5%, codeine/tramadol 24/18/32, paracetamol 600/720 mg, BPI 5.4 and 6, NNT 6 and 5, 33% and 37.5%); every MCQ has exactly one correct key. No tab or control characters, literal unicode escapes, placeholder steps or garbled text were found. Only four minor points remain (a partly unverified lipid trigger wording, MH outside the stated objectives, unverified NICE attribution for topical lidocaine, and DAS Plan C wording). Confidence is good, but this is an AI review only: the course still needs a subject-matter expert (anaesthetist and pain specialist) before clinical reliance, particularly for the LAST, adrenaline and local anaesthetic dose content.

issues.problem: The scenario is an isolated generalised seizure after a brachial plexus block, but the marking guide ties lipid to 'cardiovascular compromise or arrest' only and the explanation calls lipid 'a specific antidote for cardiovascular toxicity'. The lipid trigger (severe toxicity, including seizure not promptly controlled) is not stated, so the question does not clearly test when to start lipid. The exact trigger in the current Association of Anaesthetists guideline is unverified here.
issues.suggestedFix: State in the marking guide and explanation when lipid is started (severe toxicity such as cardiovascular compromise, arrest, or seizure/neurological features not promptly controlled) after checking the current Association of Anaesthetists LAST guideline.

issues.problem: Malignant hyperthermia (lesson paragraph, summary point, q005) is still not covered by any of the three unit objectives (anaphylaxis and aspiration; causes of intraoperative hypotension; monitoring standards). The dose content is now correct (dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg) but the topic is outside the stated scope.
issues.suggestedFix: Add an objective such as 'Recognise malignant hyperthermia and outline first-line management' or move the MH content out of this unit.

issues.problem: The lesson text names only topical capsaicin cream as the NICE-supported topical option, but the drug table ('Topical capsaicin or lidocaine') and q009 marking guide ('Topical capsaicin or lidocaine as options') present lidocaine alongside it. NICE CG173 support for topical lidocaine is unverified.
issues.suggestedFix: Verify the NICE CG173 position on topical lidocaine and either attribute it correctly (for example as a specialist or off-guideline option) or restrict the NICE-based wording and the marking guide to capsaicin cream.

issues.problem: The Plan C row says 'decide to wake the patient or proceed'. In DAS guidance Plan C is a final attempt at facemask ventilation with full neuromuscular blockade; if successful the plan is to wake the patient, and if it fails CICO is declared and Plan D follows. 'Proceed' blurs this and q008 relies on Plan C failing. Unverified against the current DAS algorithm.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword Plan C to 'final attempt at facemask ventilation with full neuromuscular blockade; if successful, wake the patient; if it fails, declare CICO and go to Plan D', and check against the current DAS algorithm.
